hints.title: Direct Node Rewiring Constraint Obstacle
hints.text: Modifying node values directly violates pure link rewiring rules. How can a sentinel node help you adjust the incoming connection to the newly swapped pair?

hints.title: Pairwise Link Reassignment Invariant
hints.text: For each adjacent node pair (A, B) preceded by prev, set prev.next to B, A.next to B.next, and B.next to A, then advance prev to A.

hints.title: Iterative Pointer Splicing Procedure
hints.text: Initialize dummy head pointing to head and set prev to dummy. While prev has at least two succeeding nodes, identify first and second. Reassign first.next to second.next, second.next to first, and prev.next to second. Advance prev to first.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def swapPairs(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        prev = dummy
        while prev.next and prev.next.next:
            first = prev.next
            second = prev.next.next
            first.next = second.next
            second.next = first
            prev.next = second
            prev = first
        return dummy.next
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Linear scan rewiring pointers pairwise in-place without recursion.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Overwriting node values directly is explicitly disallowed by problem rules requiring actual pointer manipulation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative 3-pointer link rewiring requires O(1) space compared to O(N) stack frames in recursive formulations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Proficiency with sentinel dummy node link maintenance and absence of lost node references.
